key_insight: A small set of attention heads helps determine whether a multimodal AI follows visual or textual evidence when the two disagree. These “arbitration heads” offer a targeted way to influence that choice at inference time.
problem_solved: Multimodal models can favor text or images even when that modality is less reliable for the task, producing unreliable answers under conflicting inputs.
method: Examine model behavior when visual and textual evidence conflict.
Identify attention heads that causally influence which modality drives the prediction.
Use these arbitration heads as targets for inference-time control; the provided abstract is truncated before the full control method is described.
impact: This work points toward more controllable multimodal systems that can prioritize appropriate evidence rather than defaulting to a preferred modality. The supplied excerpt does not include quantitative results or enough detail to assess practical performance.

paper_title: Beyond Modality Preference: Controlling Multimodal Arbitration under Modality Conflict in MLLMs
paper_authors: Zhaoying Pan, Shenyu Lu, Jun Hui Wong, Junyi Chai, Xiaoqian Wang
